historical_draft_passages.text: Data were collected from two sources. For the training and validation sets, gesture data were recorded by the research team using a standard webcam under varied but controlled conditions, including different lighting levels and slight variations in signer position following practices established in recent sign language dataset construction studies [24], [25]. Each gesture was captured as still frames extracted from short video sequences, yielding 300 images per class. For the independent test set, 50 video clips per class were sourced from an existing public BISINDO repository on Kaggle [26] and converted to frames using the same extraction pipeline. The total dataset therefore contains 350 samples per class, with 300 self-recorded samples used for training and validation, and 50 Kaggle-sourced samples reserved exclusively for testing.

historical_draft_passages.path: 07_dokumen\draft_paper\Effect of Training Set Expansion on YOLOv26 Performance for Real-Time BISINDO Phrase Recognition.md
historical_draft_passages.text: The Kaggle test dataset was originally collected in MP4 video format, published by Pardede [26] and contains 40 BISINDO words with approximately 50 video clips per word. Since YOLO26 operates on static image frames rather than raw video sequences, all test videos were initially converted to individual frames using OpenCV's video capture pipeline. Frames were sampled at a uniform interval to reduce redundancy from consecutive near-identical frames, a commonly adopted practice in sign language video preprocessing [27], [28], [29]. Blurry or transitional frames were eliminated; only those with distinct hand gestures were kept. For each of the eight target phrases, this procedure produced 50 suitable image samples per class, which made up the independent test set.

historical_draft_passages.path: 07_dokumen\draft_paper\Effect of Training Set Expansion on YOLOv26 Performance for Real-Time BISINDO Phrase Recognition.md
historical_draft_passages.text: The annotated dataset was divided into three non-overlapping subsets. The self-recorded dataset of 300 images per class was split into a training set and a validation set at an 80:20 ratio, insisting on 240 training samples and 60 validation samples per class. The Kaggle-sourced dataset of 50 images per class was reserved exclusively as the independent test set and was not used at any point during training or validation. This design ensures that test set performance reflects genuine generalization to unseen data from an independent source, strengthening the validity of the comparative evaluation.
